topic: Mastering the Art of Counting: Grouping and Tallying Animals

sections.title: The Big Scramble: Identifying the Problem
lecture_lines: Look at all these jumping animals!
It is hard to count them while they move.
How many elephants do you see?
animations: Scatter 15 animal icons (lions, penguins, elephants) across the screen and animate them with a continuous rhythmic 'jump' (up and down motion).
The animal icons begin to move in random directions while still jumping, increasing the visual chaos.
Pulse a thin red (#FF0000) circle around two different elephants sequentially as they move to illustrate the difficulty of counting.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Sorting by Attributes
lecture_lines: Let's group them by their kind!
Lions go to the yellow box.
Penguins and elephants find their homes too.
animations: Draw three rectangular boxes at the bottom with labels and outlines: Yellow (#FFFF00) for Lions, White (#FFFFFF) for Penguins, and Grey (#808080) for Elephants.
All lion icons [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lion.svg] move smoothly from the chaotic group into the yellow box.
All penguin icons and elephant icons move simultaneously into their respective white and grey boxes.

sections.title: The One-to-One Marking Method
lecture_lines: Use a mark for each animal counted.
The fifth mark crosses through the group.
This helps us not skip any animals.
We have five penguins in total.
animations: As the first penguin in the box is highlighted, a single vertical white (#FFFFFF) tally mark appears in a sidebar.
Three more vertical white (#FFFFFF) tally marks appear one by one as the second, third, and fourth penguins are highlighted.
The fifth penguin is highlighted, and a diagonal white (#FFFFFF) line is drawn across the four existing tally marks.
The completed tally group and the five penguins in the box flash white (#FFFFFF) together.
The number '5' appears in white (#FFFFFF) above the tally group to confirm the count.

sections.title: Visualizing Data: The Animal Pictograph
lecture_lines: Let's turn our marks into colored blocks.
Stack three yellow blocks for the lions.
Five black blocks show our five penguins.
Two grey blocks stand for the elephants.
Now we have a clear animal chart.
animations: The tally marks for each animal group morph into small colored squares corresponding to their group color (#FFFF00, #404040, #808080).
Three yellow (#FFFF00) blocks stack vertically above a 'Lions' label.
Five dark grey (#404040) blocks stack vertically above a 'Penguins' label.
Two light grey (#808080) blocks stack vertically above an 'Elephants' label.
The three stacks align horizontally on a common base to form a clean pictograph.

sections.title: Comparison and Verification
lecture_lines: Which animal group is the tallest?
Penguins have the most, elephants have the least.
Ten animals in total are all accounted for!
animations: The penguin [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/penguin.svg] block stack (the tallest) scales up and down slightly and glows with a white (#FFFFFF) border.

The penguin [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/penguin.svg] stack highlights in green (#00FF00) and the elephant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/elephant.svg] stack (the shortest) highlights in red (#FF0000).
The digits 3, 5, and 2 float from the top of their stacks to the screen center, forming the equation '3 + 5 + 2 = 10' in white (#FFFFFF).
